title: The Blue Compass
verdict: Noelle Cross was responsible for the disappearance of a sealed donor letter.
intent: Noelle Cross wanted to hide a forged citation record before the donor family compared the documents.
The culprit needed delayed discovery so the object could pass the first search and be recovered later.
action_schema: Use role-specific access: the archive coordinator carried the only key that opened the back side of the display case.
Remove a sealed donor letter from its checked location.
Hide the item in a hollow catalog box stored behind the reference desk.
Allow incomplete suspicion to fall on distractor suspects.
evidence_cues: a sealed donor letter disappeared from the north wing of a university archive during a donor exhibition.
The object was confirmed present before the relevant disturbance.

The relevant tool or mechanism was a white cotton glove with blue ink on the thumb.
The item could be concealed in a hollow catalog box stored behind the reference desk.
The hiding place required insider knowledge because only the archive coordinator knew that several catalog boxes had hollow conservation inserts.
